characters.name: Anselm Voss-Rietveld
characters.line: I could brief Capital myself. They remember me from training.

characters.name: Pavel Oskarsen
characters.line: I have seen six ambassadors. Five also thought a promise was a reservation.

characters.name: Sola Dewrin
characters.line: I can make the calls. But I am not everybody’s translator and emergency exit.

characters.name: Elise
characters.line: The Minister could visit our project. Provided we remember the people, not just the photograph.

characters.name: Bianca Montefiore
characters.line: A convoy needs vehicles, not a beautifully formatted spreadsheet.

characters.name: Ines Thibault-Lund
characters.line: Four hundred people in the queue. No, they do not disappear when the Minister arrives.

characters.name: Lucien Falk
characters.line: A good photograph is worth a thousand words. Legal would prefer zero.

characters.name: Maxim
characters.line: I made a checklist of the checklists. Is that useful?

characters.name: Ketu Marrimba
characters.line: I can feed the delegation. I cannot feed its ego.

characters.name: Director Ndao
characters.line: Permission has three stamps. You have submitted two and a coffee stain.

characters.name: Celeste Norren
characters.line: Before you mention 17.6%, yes, we have counted the biscuits.

characters.name: Marcel Deux
characters.line: Everything is possible. The question is who owes whom afterwards.

characters.name: Ruth Vale
characters.line: Off the record is an agreement, not something you say after the quote.

characters.name: Minister Bako
characters.line: An appointment? My secretary says I am unavailable. My caddie disagrees.

characters.name: Dr Amara Chen
characters.line: We can support the programme. We cannot promise six agencies will agree on one logo.

venues.name: Embassy kitchen
venues.description: Staff coffee and a lunch assembled by Ketu.

venues.name: Chez Marcel
venues.description: Classic French and Italian dining. Quiet tables, serious cutlery.

venues.name: Auntie’s Courtyard
venues.description: Local cuisine, open-air tables and conversations that travel.

venues.name: The Gilded Palm
venues.description: Rooftop chandeliers, imported everything, a very visible bill.

venues.name: Mizu
venues.description: Sushi, minimalist surroundings and ambitious small plates.

venues.name: The Quiet Amendment
venues.description: A discreet bar with food and excessively well-informed regulars.

locations.name: Embassy
locations.description: Your team, your in-tray, your responsibility.

locations.name: Foreign Ministry / Protocol
locations.description: Appointments, landing permissions and wounded precedence.

locations.name: EU Delegation
locations.description: Coordination, contested clauses and exactly 17.6% of the refreshments.

locations.name: The Quiet Amendment
locations.description: Rumours and favours that never quite stay unofficial.

locations.name: Press Correspondents Club
locations.description: Access, credibility and the dangerous phrase “off the record”.

locations.name: Precedence Golf Club
locations.description: The people who never answer letters are available on the ninth green.

locations.name: UN House & multilateral circuit
locations.description: Programmes, funding, mandates and competing logos.

opening.text: {line} What do you want to discuss?

choices.label: How are things going, really?
What would help you do your job?
Capital expects results. No excuses.

listen.text: People will work with you if you notice what it costs them. Public credit would be a start.

choices.label: You will get the credit. I’ll back you publicly.
choices.result: Your promise of public credit makes the team more willing to share information.

choices.label: Let’s keep personal feelings out of this.
choices.result: The conversation ends politely. Cooperation becomes rather less enthusiastic.

support.text: A clear brief, realistic time and no surprise overtime. Can you manage that?

choices.label: Agreed. We’ll protect your time.
choices.result: Clear boundaries earn trust and reduce friction with the rest of the team.

choices.label: Help now; I’ll owe you a favour.
choices.result: A favour is accepted. It will not be forgotten.

pressure.text: You can order compliance. You cannot order enthusiasm. Is that what you want?

choices.label: Fair point. Let’s agree priorities.
choices.result: You step back from the threat and agree workable priorities.

choices.label: Yes. Have it ready, or explain yourself to HQ.
choices.result: The instruction is accepted. Trust and cooperation suffer.

events.title: Your presence is requested immediately
events.text: The host ministry unveils a plaque in twenty minutes. Your absence would be noticed. Your schedule is not their concern.

choices.label: Attend personally — replace your planned activity
choices.result: You attend the ceremony. Your planned work must wait.

choices.label: Send Anselm with a strict brief
choices.result: Anselm represents the mission. The strict brief limits his promises.

choices.label: Decline diplomatically
choices.result: Protocol records your absence with considerable courtesy.

events.title: Two briefings, no shared facts
events.text: Pavel and Anselm each wrote a briefing and refuse to combine them. The Minister cannot hold two contradictory positions.

choices.label: Give Pavel the lead and Anselm visible credit
choices.result: A clear lead and shared credit begin repairing the Pavel–Anselm feud.

choices.label: Order them to cooperate
choices.result: One document appears. They stop speaking to each other.

events.title: The generous supplier · part I
events.text: A caterer offers an unusually cheap reception. Sola recognises the surname. Investigate or take the bargain?

choices.label: Ask Sola to check the ownership
choices.result: Sola begins tracing the supplier. A follow-up will arrive tomorrow.

choices.label: Accept the offer without questions
choices.result: The bargain is accepted. Its strings will become apparent later.

events.title: The generous supplier · part II
events.text: The company belongs to a protocol official’s cousin. A correspondent has started asking about the reception.

choices.label: Disclose the connection and change supplier
choices.result: Transparent procurement costs more but prevents a scandal.

choices.label: Keep the deal quiet
choices.result: The cousin is delighted. Capital is less amused by the eventual questions.

events.title: A project, not a photo opportunity
events.text: Elise wants the Minister to meet project beneficiaries, not merely unveil a donor plaque. UN partners demand their own speaking slots.

choices.label: Protect time for beneficiaries
choices.result: Elise negotiates a useful project segment with the UN partners.

choices.label: Prioritise the Minister’s photograph
choices.result: The photograph is secured. Elise remembers what you valued.

events.title: The 17.6% entitlement
events.text: Celeste slides the biscuit plate towards you. “Your national allocation, colleague.” The room braces itself.

choices.label: “Naturally, 17.6% of the coffee too.”
choices.result: Pained expressions all round. Your self-deprecation briefly softens the coalition.

choices.label: Save the joke and discuss the clause
choices.result: The room agrees on the clause. Nobody misses the joke quite enough to admit it.

events.title: A casual quote
events.text: Ruth asks whether the Minister’s visit is really confirmed. The microphone looks switched off. It is not.

choices.label: Explain what is confirmed and what is pending
choices.result: Your careful distinction survives the headline.

choices.label: Everything is entirely ready
choices.result: The claim is printed. Somebody checks it.
